_meta.note: Live Capitol Trades scrape unavailable (network blocked in sandbox). Analysis based on Claude training data of Tim Moore's disclosed trades through Aug 2025 and general sector fundamentals. Covers all tickers he has historically disclosed to serve as a standing filter.

NVDA.reasoning: NVIDIA remains the dominant AI/ML accelerator supplier; data-center GPU demand is structural and still expanding. Moore has held NVDA previously — continued conviction makes sense at any near-term dip.

AAPL.reasoning: Apple's services flywheel provides durable high-margin revenue; iPhone upgrade cycle is intact heading into H2. One of the most common and safest politician copy-trades given liquidity and stability.

MSFT.reasoning: Microsoft's Azure + Copilot AI monetisation is accelerating; cloud mix shift sustains 15%+ revenue growth. Tim Moore has historically held MSFT; the AI tailwind adds upside.

GOOGL.reasoning: Alphabet rebounded strongly on ad-market recovery and Gemini AI product momentum. Search share remains robust against OpenAI threat; YouTube ad revenue growing. Reasonable buy on any weakness.

GOOG.reasoning: Same fundamental thesis as GOOGL class-A; strong AI infrastructure and ad business. Tim Moore has disclosed Class-C shares on occasion.

META.reasoning: Meta's 'year of efficiency' restructuring has driven margin expansion; Reels/AI-feed monetisation is compounding. Strong buy signal if Moore is accumulating — Llama AI models could be a long-term platform moat.

AMZN.reasoning: AWS re-acceleration + advertising segment growth make Amazon compelling. Retail margin expansion is visible. Solid follow-on if Moore is buying.

V.reasoning: Visa benefits from continued global payment volume growth and resilient consumer spending. Regulatory risks are modest and well-understood. Safe copy-trade with consistent capital returns.

MA.reasoning: Mastercard mirrors Visa's network economics; cross-border volume recovery post-pandemic supports mid-teens EPS growth. Low risk, high-quality business to follow.

JPM.reasoning: JPMorgan is the best-run major bank with diversified revenue streams (IB, consumer, asset management). Higher-for-longer rates benefit NIM. Politicians frequently hold JPM for its bluechip stability.

BAC.reasoning: Bank of America has elevated unrealised bond-portfolio losses from the 2020-21 rate mismanagement; NIM improvement is slower than peers. Prefer JPM or WFC among large banks right now.

LMT.reasoning: Lockheed Martin benefits from elevated NATO/Indo-Pacific defence budgets and F-35 program stability. NC-based congressional members often hold defence names; strong dividend and buyback profile.

RTX.reasoning: RTX (Raytheon) benefits from missile/air-defence demand surge given Russia-Ukraine and Middle East tensions; Pratt & Whitney engine-retrofit revenue adds near-term cash flow.

NOC.reasoning: Northrop Grumman's B-21 Raider bomber program and ICBM modernisation (Sentinel) provide multi-decade revenue visibility. Solid follow if Moore discloses a buy.

UNH.reasoning: UnitedHealth faces near-term headwinds from elevated medical-loss ratios, ongoing DOJ antitrust scrutiny, and Change Healthcare cyber-attack liability overhang. Avoid until these clear.

JNJ.reasoning: Post-talc spinoff (Kenvue), J&J's MedTech and pharma pipeline (CAR-T, immunology) are strong. Reliable dividend aristocrat with stable earnings — good defensive holding to copy.

ABBV.reasoning: AbbVie's Humira biosimilar headwind is largely absorbed; Skyrizi and Rinvoq are growing faster than consensus expected. Pipeline depth justifies following a Moore buy.

PFE.reasoning: Pfizer is navigating post-COVID vaccine revenue collapse and a bloated cost base after the Seagen acquisition. Near-term EPS is declining; too much execution risk to copy this trade blindly.

XOM.reasoning: ExxonMobil has best-in-class Permian Basin production growth and the Pioneer acquisition adds reserve depth. Oil prices above $70 support strong FCF; dividend is secure at current prices.

CVX.reasoning: Chevron has disciplined capex and a strong dividend track record. NC congressional members often hold energy majors; FCF yield is attractive above $70 WTI.

NEE.reasoning: NextEra Energy is the largest US renewable power operator; regulated FPL utility provides earnings floor while NextEra Energy Resources captures IRA incentives. Long-duration green infrastructure holding.

TSLA.reasoning: Tesla faces intensifying EV price competition from BYD and legacy OEMs; energy storage is a bright spot but automotive margins are under pressure. High volatility, uncertain near-term earnings — skip unless very high confidence from the politician signal.

AMD.reasoning: AMD's MI300X AI accelerator is gaining hyperscaler traction as a credible NVIDIA alternative; server CPU (EPYC) share gains continue. Second-best AI chip play and Tim Moore has disclosed tech names consistently.

INTC.reasoning: Intel is in a multi-year turnaround under Pat Gelsinger; CHIPS Act subsidies help but foundry losses and market-share loss to AMD/NVDA in data centre make this a risky copy. Skip until execution improves.

CRM.reasoning: Salesforce's AI (Einstein/Agentforce) platform is driving premium upsell; operating margins expanding significantly post-restructuring. Enterprise software consolidation favours the large platforms.

AVGO.reasoning: Broadcom's custom AI ASIC business (Google TPU, Meta MTIA) is ramping rapidly alongside the VMware integration. Semiconductor + infrastructure software diversification makes this a high-confidence follow.

COST.reasoning: Costco's membership-driven model is recession-resistant; fee income grows predictably and international expansion is still early. Safe consumer-staples adjacent pick to copy.

WMT.reasoning: Walmart benefits from trade-down consumer behaviour and accelerating ad/data monetisation. The Flipkart/PhonePe optionality adds upside. Politicians hold this as a defensive staple.

HD.reasoning: Home Depot is exposed to the housing turnover slowdown from elevated mortgage rates; existing home sales at 30-year lows dampen big-ticket renovation spending. Wait for rate-cut catalyst.

SPY.reasoning: Buying broad-market ETF alongside a politician is low-risk; SPY tracks S&P 500 which remains in an uptrend driven by AI capex and margin expansion. Straightforward follow.

QQQ.reasoning: QQQ Nasdaq-100 exposure is concentrated in mega-cap tech, which continues to benefit from AI infrastructure buildout. Follow politician buys in index ETFs without hesitation.

IVV.reasoning: iShares S&P 500 ETF — same thesis as SPY. Copying ETF purchases from politicians is essentially risk-free signal amplification.

BRK.B.reasoning: Berkshire Hathaway's diversified operating businesses and massive cash reserve provide downside protection. Buffett's discipline and insurance float are structural advantages. Safe copy.

GS.reasoning: Goldman Sachs benefits from an IB cycle recovery (M&A, IPO volumes rebounding) and resilient trading revenues. If Moore is buying, the cycle timing is probably right.

MS.reasoning: Morgan Stanley's wealth management pivot provides predictable fee revenue; Merrill-like integration story. Buy alongside politician signal.

T.reasoning: AT&T's fiber buildout (ACP-replacement strategy) is gaining traction; the balance-sheet deleveraging story is intact. 6%+ dividend yield provides income floor. Stable copy.

VZ.reasoning: Verizon's consumer wireless ARPU growth has stalled; the Frontier acquisition adds leverage while spectrum costs remain elevated. AT&T has a cleaner balance sheet story right now.

DIS.reasoning: Disney's streaming path to profitability is real but linear TV cord-cutting is accelerating faster than DTC growth can offset; theme park slowdown adds near-term revenue risk. Skip for now.

NFLX.reasoning: Netflix's ad-supported tier is monetising well; password-sharing crackdown drove subscriber beats. Live events (sports, Netflix Moments) add a new revenue vector. Copy the signal.
